Rumors suggest Apple is set to announce new products on October 13. Based on Apple's typical timing for October events, here's an estimate of when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

Apple's September events follow a regular pattern, but the timing of its October events is harder to pin down — both the event dates and the lead-up periods before announcements have varied considerably.

Since 2010, Apple has held just 10 October events, with the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Here's a look at the lead-up periods for each October event since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg recently reported that Apple plans to announce the long-rumored smart home hub, the next-generation HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K with next-gen Siri AI features on Tuesday, October 13 — though the report didn't mention whether Apple will hold an event to unveil these products.

If accurate, Apple could announce the event date as early as next Monday, October 5, or as late as Wednesday, October 7.

It's worth noting that Apple is also expected to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a refreshed iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including touch-screen versions) in 2026. Whether these products will debut at the same event, be unveiled at a separate event, or simply be announced via press release remains unknown.

Then again, in October 2024, Apple unveiled new Macs over three consecutive days through press releases; similarly, in October 2025, Apple skipped holding an event entirely and instead directly announced the M5 chip along with new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro models.

By comparison, Apple has historically held just one November event — way back in November 2020, when its "One More Thing" event introduced the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was an unusual year for Apple's event calendar. In addition to a rare late-June WWDC, Apple also held separate events in both September and October that year, all due to COVID-19 disrupting the typical schedule.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
